mainTopic: The אתרוג's new year in שבט, and its status for מעשר and ביעור when it crosses the שמיטה year
overview: The גמרא first corrects רבה בר רב הונא's statement. According to רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג goes by its picking (לקיטה) like a ירק, but its new year is still שבט, like a tree. A side question asks why the ברייתא chose the example of the third year going into the fourth. The answer is that handling damages an אתרוג tree, so after שביעית it bears no proper fruit for three years. רבי יוחנן then learns from רבי ינאי that the new year is the lunar month of שבט, and it stays there even in a leap year. רבה and רב המנונא disagree about an אתרוג that forms in one year and is picked in the next, across the שמיטה boundary. רבה explains to אביי that the sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית is exempt from מעשר because it is הפקר. A ברייתא of רבי שמעון seems to contradict them both. The גמרא answers that this is a dispute among תנאים and brings the testimony of the five elders and the vote at אושא. The amud ends by asking why שביעית was mentioned at all, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא gives the אתרוג a new year in שבט, even though it follows רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The view that the אתרוג goes by לקיטה is רבן גמליאל's. Yet that same ברייתא says the אתרוג's new year is שבט. This contradicts רבה בר רב הונא, who said that for רבן גמליאל it is תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who is the one you heard say that the אתרוג follows the time of picking? It is רבן גמליאל. And yet the ברייתא teaches שבט!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבה בר רב הונא's earlier statement. It points out that a ברייתא clearly following רבן גמליאל's view still puts the אתרוג's new year in שבט, not תשרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה בר רב הונא had reasoned this way: since רבן גמליאל treats the אתרוג like a ירק (it goes by לקיטה), its new year should also be תשרי, like a ירק. But the ברייתא about picking an אתרוג on the eve of ט״ו בשבט uses the picking-time rule, which only רבן גמליאל holds. That same ברייתא sets the cutoff at שבט. So it seems רבן גמליאל himself keeps שבט as the new year.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom have you heard say this? (a formula that identifies whose opinion a source follows)
Picking. The time the fruit is harvested.
Goes after; follows (that point in time)
It teaches (the ברייתא states)
The month of Shevat. Its 15th day is the new year for trees.

steps.confusionAlert: Two separate questions are at stake here. (1) Which moment decides the year's tithes: the picking (לקיטה) or the budding (חנטה)? (2) On what date does the year switch over: תשרי or שבט? רבן גמליאל uses picking for question 1. That does not automatically mean תשרי for question 2.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
that goes after the time of picking?
Rabban Gamliel.
And yet it teaches Shevat!
phrases.notes: The ברייתא about picking an אתרוג on the eve of the 15th of Shevat

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאָזֵיל בָּתַר לְקִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה בר רב הונא's statement on the previous amud, that רבן גמליאל gives the אתרוג a new year in תשרי
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה בר רב הונא's claim that for רבן גמליאל the אתרוג's new year is תשרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא uses the לקיטה rule, which is only רבן גמליאל's view. It still sets the new year at שבט. So רבן גמליאל cannot hold תשרי.

steps.title: רבה בר רב הונא's statement is rephrased: picking like a ירק, but new year in שבט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רבה בר רב הונא's teaching. רבן גמליאל uses לקיטה like a ירק, but the אתרוג's new year still stays in שבט, like a tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said. רבה בר רב הונא said: even though רבן גמליאל said the אתרוג goes by picking like a vegetable, its new year is שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the challenge was too strong, the גמרא rewrites what רבה בר רב הונא must have actually said. The new version matches the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original version tied the two issues together: picking like a ירק, so new year like a ירק (תשרי). The fixed version separates them. רבן גמליאל borrows only the picking rule from ירק. On the date of the new year, the אתרוג stays a tree and switches in שבט.

keyTerms.meaning: If it was said, this is how it was said (a correction of a statement's wording)
Even though
Vegetable. Its tithe year goes by picking, and its new year is תשרי.
New year (here, for the purpose of tithes)

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג is a mix of both categories. It goes by לקיטה like a ירק, but its new year is שבט like a tree.

phrases.english: Rather, if it was said, this is how it was said:
Rabba bar Rav Huna said:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל
phrases.english: Even though Rabban Gamliel said
that an etrog goes after picking, like a vegetable,
its new year is Shevat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge by rewording the original statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the version of the statement (אי אתמר הכי אתמר)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבן גמליאל treats the אתרוג fully like a ירק, so its new year would be תשרי
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן גמליאל borrows only the picking rule from ירק. The new year stays in שבט.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבן גמליאל, the אתרוג goes by לקיטה, but its new year is שבט

steps.title: Why do the two ברייתות use different year examples?
steps.stepSummary: The ירק ברייתא uses the second year going into the third. The אתרוג ברייתא uses the third going into the fourth. Why the difference?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different there, that it teaches 'if it was the second year going into the third,' and what is different here, that it teaches 'if it was the third year going into the fourth'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a side question about wording: why did the two ברייתות choose different years as examples? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples could show the same point. In both, the year changes from one kind of tithe to another, such as מעשר שני to מעשר עני. The years with מעשר שני are the 1st, 2nd, 4th and 5th. The years with מעשר עני are the 3rd and 6th. So second→third works just as well as third→fourth. The גמרא wants to know why the אתרוג ברייתא chose a different pair of years.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different?
There / here
Entering (going into the next year)

phrases.english: What is different there, that it teaches
"if it was the second year going into the third"
phrases.notes: The ברייתא about ירק picked on the eve of ראש השנה

phrases.english: and what is different here, that it teaches
"if it was the third year going into the fourth"?
phrases.notes: The ברייתא about an אתרוג picked on the eve of ט״ו בשבט

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new side question about the wording of the ברייתא
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the אתרוג ברייתא use the third→fourth year example instead of second→third?

steps.title: The ברייתא teaches in passing that the אתרוג tree is harmed by handling
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא slips in a farming fact. Handling damages an אתרוג tree. Since everyone handles it in שביעית, it does not bear proper fruit for three years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us something in passing. Handling is harmful to an אתרוג. Since everyone handles it during שביעית, it does not produce fruit for three years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the choice of years was on purpose. It quietly teaches a fact about how the אתרוג tree grows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית, all fields are ownerless, so many people touch and pick the אתרוג trees, and this damages them. As a result, the tree gives no good fruit in the first and second years after שביעית. The first realistic picking is in the third year. So the ברייתא used the case of the third year going into the fourth.

keyTerms.term: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us something extra, in passing
The hand (handling) is harmful to it
They handle / touch it
The seventh year (שמיטה), when fields are ownerless

steps.whatToRemember: The different years in the two ברייתות were chosen deliberately. Because of handling in שביעית, an אתרוג tree only bears real fruit again in the third year of the cycle.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new הלכה about tithes. It is a farming fact that explains why the ברייתא chose its example.

phrases.aramaic: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן,
phrases.english: It teaches us a matter in passing:
that handling is harmful to an etrog,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַיְּידֵי דִּמְמַשְׁמְשִׁי בֵּיהּ כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בִּשְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: and since everyone handles it in the Sabbatical Year,

phrases.aramaic: לָא טָעֵין פֵּרֵי עַד תְּלָת שְׁנִין.
phrases.english: it does not bear fruit until three years.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִילְּתָא אַגַּב אוֹרְחֵיהּ קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the different year examples
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The third→fourth example reflects reality. After שביעית, an אתרוג tree does not fruit until the third year, because of the damage from handling.

steps.title: When is the new year of an אתרוג?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks רבי ינאי on what date the new year of an אתרוג falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: For an אתרוג, when is its new year?
steps.whatsHappening: A new section opens with a direct question. רבי יוחנן wants to know the exact date of the אתרוג's new year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this already showed that the אתרוג keeps a tree-style new year, not a vegetable-style one. Now the question is practical: on what date does it actually fall? The answer decides which year's rules apply to a given אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him (a real question, looking for information)
Citron, the fruit used on סוכות
New year (here: the cut-off date that decides which year a fruit belongs to)
When?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan asked Rabbi Yannai:
phrases.notes: רבי ינאי was רבי יוחנן's teacher.

phrases.english: An etrog — when is its new year?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the farming explanation to pinning down the exact date of the אתרוג's new year.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The date of the אתרוג's new year.

steps.title: The answer: שבט
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that the אתרוג's new year is in שבט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי gives a short answer: שבט. This matches the general new year for trees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The אתרוג follows the same new year as other trees. That fits the ברייתא from earlier in the sugya. But the one-word answer leaves something unclear, and the next step asks about it.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of Shevat, the new year for trees

phrases.english: He said to him: Shevat.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The אתרוג's new year is in שבט.

steps.title: Which שבט: calendar month or solar season?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן asks whether 'שבט' means the calendar month or the solar season called שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you mean שבט of the months, or שבט of the season?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן asks a follow-up question. The word 'שבט' could mean two different time periods.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'שבט of the months' is the lunar month on the Jewish calendar. 'שבט of the season' is a period counted by the sun, starting a fixed time after the winter turning point. It falls on a different lunar date each year. The two can be weeks apart, so the answer matters for real fruit.

keyTerms.meaning: Months (the lunar calendar months)
Season counted by the sun

steps.confusionAlert: 'שבט of the season' is not a month on our calendar. It is a solar time-period that only loosely lines up with the lunar month of שבט.

phrases.english: Shevat of the months, or Shevat of the season?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies what the answer in step 6 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'שבט' means the lunar month or the solar season.

steps.title: The lunar month
steps.stepSummary: רבי ינאי answers that he means the lunar calendar month of שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: of the months.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ינאי clarifies that he means the regular calendar month of שבט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new year is set by the Jewish calendar, not by the position of the sun. This makes it a fixed, easy-to-know date.

phrases.english: He said to him: of the months.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the follow-up question of step 7.

steps.title: What happens in a leap year?
steps.stepSummary: Either רבא asked רב נחמן, or רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי: in a leap year, does the date shift?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked רב נחמן (and some say רבי יוחנן asked רבי ינאי): If it was a leap year, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the lunar month counts, a new question follows. What happens in a leap year, which has an extra month?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A leap year adds a second אדר, so the calendar months sit about a month earlier compared to the seasons. Perhaps the new year should move later, to stay at the same point in the growing season. Or perhaps it stays in שבט. The גמרא also records two versions of who asked this question.

keyTerms.meaning: Leap year (a year with an extra month of אדר)
And some say (another version of who said it)
What is the law?

phrases.english: Rava asked Rav Nachman,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מֵרַבִּי יַנַּאי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rabbi Yochanan who asked Rabbi Yannai:
If it was a leap year, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the lunar-month answer by asking about years with an extra month.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the אתרוג's new year moves in a leap year.

steps.title: Follow the majority of years
steps.stepSummary: The answer: follow the usual pattern of most years, so the new year stays in שבט.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Go after the majority of years.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer is that a leap year does not change anything. We follow what happens in most years, which are regular years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most years are not leap years, and in those years the new year is in שבט. So even in a leap year it stays in שבט and does not move to the first אדר. One fixed rule applies every year.

keyTerms.meaning: Go after the majority

steps.whatToRemember: The אתרוג's new year is the lunar month of שבט, and it stays in שבט even in a leap year.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב שָׁנִים.
phrases.english: He said to him: Go after the majority of years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַלֵּךְ אַחַר רוֹב שָׁנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the leap-year question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Follow the majority of years, so the new year stays in שבט.

steps.title: רבה's rule for an אתרוג crossing the שמיטה boundary
steps.stepSummary: רבה rules on two cases. An אתרוג from the sixth year picked in שביעית is exempt from מעשר and from ביעור. An אתרוג from שביעית picked in the eighth year is exempt from מעשר but obligated in ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: An אתרוג of the sixth year that entered the seventh is exempt from מעשר and exempt from ביעור. An אתרוג of the seventh year that entered the eighth is exempt from מעשר and obligated in ביעור.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה gives a new teaching. It covers an אתרוג whose life crosses the line into or out of the שמיטה year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Of the sixth year' means the fruit formed (חנטה) in year six. 'Entered the seventh' means it was picked (לקיטה) in year seven. In the first case it is exempt from ביעור, because it formed in year six. It is also exempt from מעשר; step 13 explains that this is because it was ownerless (הפקר) during שביעית, not because the picking year decides. In the second case the fruit formed in שביעית, so it has no מעשר and is obligated in ביעור like שמיטה produce.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year, the שמיטה year
Tithes (not taken from שמיטה produce)
Removing שמיטה produce from the house once that crop is gone from the fields
Fruit 'of the sixth year' (formed in year six)

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the two different measuring points. 'Of the sixth year' refers to when the fruit formed. 'Entered the seventh' refers to when it was picked.

phrases.english: Rabba said:
An etrog of the sixth year that entered into the seventh —
phrases.notes: It formed in year six and was picked in year seven.

phrases.english: is exempt from tithes
and exempt from removal.
And one of the seventh year that entered into the eighth —
phrases.notes: It formed in שביעית and was picked in year eight.

phrases.english: is exempt from tithes and obligated in removal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: אֶתְרוֹג בַּת שִׁשִּׁית שֶׁנִּכְנְסָה לִשְׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the new-year date to how the אתרוג's unusual status plays out in שמיטה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Formed in year six and picked in year seven: exempt from מעשר and from ביעור. Formed in year seven and picked in year eight: exempt from מעשר and obligated in ביעור.

steps.title: אביי: the first case is lenient both ways
steps.stepSummary: אביי accepts the second case. But he asks how the first case can be exempt from ביעור, which follows formation, and also exempt from מעשר, which would follow picking.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: The second case makes sense, because it is a stringency. But the first case, exempt from ביעור — why? Because we say to follow formation. If so, it should be obligated in מעשר!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה. He accepts the second case but attacks the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the second case, following formation leads to the strict result of ביעור, which is reasonable. In the first case, the exemption from ביעור only works if we follow formation, which was in year six. But a fruit formed in year six is regular produce, so it should owe מעשר. רבה seems to follow formation for one law and picking for the other, and both choices come out lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, this part makes sense (it sets up 'but' the problem part)
The last clause / the first clause
As a stringency
The formation of the fruit
If so

steps.whyThisMatters: It is hard to justify using two different measuring systems in one case so that both come out lenient. רבה must now explain the first case consistently.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Granted the latter clause — it is a stringency,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רֵישָׁא פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר — אַמַּאי?
phrases.english: but the first clause, exempt from removal — why?
Because we say: go after the formation;
if so, it should be obligated in tithes!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁלָמָא סֵיפָא לְחוּמְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the first case of רבה's rule in step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first case of רבה's rule: exempt from both מעשר and ביעור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ביעור exemption depends on following formation (year six). By that same measure the fruit is ordinary sixth-year produce and should owe מעשר. Exempting it from both is lenient by two opposite measures.

steps.title: רבה Explains: Everyone Touches It, So It Is Ownerless
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers אביי. The sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית is exempt from מעשר because during שביעית the fruit is open to everyone and counts as הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Everyone's hand touches it, and you say it should be obligated in tithes?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה answers אביי's challenge from the previous step. He explains why his first case is exempt from מעשר even though its formation is in the sixth year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argued that if the ביעור exemption follows formation (year six), then the same measure makes this ordinary sixth-year fruit, so it should owe מעשר. רבה answers that the מעשר exemption has a different source. During שביעית everyone is allowed to enter and touch the fruit, so it becomes הפקר, and ownerless produce is exempt from מעשר. So רבה can follow formation consistently, and the מעשר exemption comes from the fruit's ownerless status, not from the picking date.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone's hand touches it. The fruit is open to the public.
Ownerless property. It is exempt from מעשר.
It should be obligated.
Tithes taken from produce.

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is NOT saying that the time of picking controls מעשר. The אתרוג is still treated as sixth-year fruit. The exemption from מעשר comes only from its ownerless (הפקר) status during שביעית.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יַד הַכֹּל מְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בָּהּ,
phrases.english: He (Rabba) said to him: Everyone's hand touches it,
phrases.notes: During the Sabbatical Year, anyone may enter the orchard and take the fruit.

phrases.english: and you say it should be obligated in tithes?!
phrases.notes: Ownerless produce is exempt from tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: יַד הַכֹּל מְמַשְׁמְשִׁין בָּהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a different reason for the exemption: הפקר status rather than the timing rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי assumed that the מעשר exemption had to come from following the time of picking, which would clash with following formation for ביעור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Formation determines the year for both laws. The מעשר exemption comes from the fruit being הפקר during שביעית.

steps.title: רב המנונא: The Fruit Always Keeps Its Original Year
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא rules that a sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית is always treated as sixth-year fruit. A שביעית אתרוג picked in the eighth year is always treated as שביעית fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב המנונא said: A sixth-year [אתרוג] that entered into the seventh year is always sixth-year. And a seventh-year [אתרוג] that entered into the eighth year is always seventh-year.
steps.whatsHappening: רב המנונא gives his own view. It disagrees with רבה about the first case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב המנונא, the year in which the fruit formed decides every law: it counts as that year's fruit 'always.' So the sixth-year אתרוג picked in שביעית is obligated in מעשר, which disagrees with רבה, and is exempt from ביעור. The שביעית אתרוג picked in the eighth year is exempt from מעשר and obligated in ביעור, which matches רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A fruit 'of the sixth year,' meaning it formed in the sixth year.
Enters, meaning it continues into the next year and is picked then.
Always, for all purposes.
The fruit's formation stage, which sets its year.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up two opinions, רבה and רב המנונא. The coming ברייתא will be tested against both of them.

phrases.english: And Rav Hamnuna said:

phrases.aramaic: בַּת שִׁשִּׁית שֶׁנִּכְנֶסֶת לִשְׁבִיעִית — לְעוֹלָם שִׁשִּׁית,
phrases.english: A sixth-year [etrog] that entered into the seventh year is always sixth-year,
phrases.notes: So it is subject to tithes and not to elimination.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַת שְׁבִיעִית הַנִּכְנֶסֶת לִשְׁמִינִית — לְעוֹלָם שְׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: and a seventh-year [etrog] that entered into the eighth year is always seventh-year.
phrases.notes: So it is exempt from tithes and subject to elimination.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opinion that differs from רבה's ruling in step 11 on the first case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Formation year controls completely. Sixth-into-seventh is sixth-year fruit: obligated in מעשר, exempt from ביעור. Seventh-into-eighth is seventh-year fruit: exempt from מעשר, obligated in ביעור.

steps.title: A ברייתא Requires Both Growth and Picking in the Obligated Year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from רבי שמעון. Both cases are exempt from מעשר and from ביעור, because an obligation applies only if the fruit both grew and was picked in the obligated year.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: A sixth-year אתרוג that entered into the seventh year is exempt from מעשר and exempt from ביעור. Nothing is obligated in מעשר unless it grew at a time of obligation and was picked at a time of obligation. And a seventh-year [אתרוג] that entered into the eighth year is exempt from מעשר and exempt from ביעור. Nothing is obligated in ביעור unless it grew in שביעית and was picked in שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא in order to challenge the opinions just stated. This step lays out the source; the next step says exactly whom it contradicts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses a 'both ends' rule. To be obligated, the fruit must have grown during the obligated period and also been picked during it. Each case crosses a year boundary, so each case is exempt from both laws. This differs from the view that only the formation year matters.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged. It introduces a source, usually a ברייתא, that contradicts an Amora.
Removing שביעית produce from the house once that crop is gone from the fields.
It grew at a time of obligation.
It was picked.

phrases.aramaic: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: They raised an objection: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
An etrog from the sixth year that entered into the seventh year

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר,
phrases.english: is exempt from tithes and exempt from elimination,
for you have nothing that is obligated in tithes

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדַל בְּחִיּוּב וְנִלְקַט בְּחִיּוּב.
phrases.english: unless it grew in a time of obligation and was picked in a time of obligation.
phrases.notes: Picking in the seventh year breaks the obligation in tithes.

phrases.english: And a seventh-year [etrog] that entered into the eighth year

phrases.aramaic: פְּטוּרָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וּפְטוּרָה מִן הַבִּיעוּר,
phrases.english: is exempt from tithes and exempt from elimination,
for you have nothing that is obligated in elimination

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן גָּדַל בִּשְׁבִיעִית וְנִלְקַט בִּשְׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: unless it grew in the seventh year and was picked in the seventh year.
phrases.notes: Picking in the eighth year breaks the obligation in elimination.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a תנאי source to test the rulings of רבה (step 11) and רב המנונא (step 14).
steps.kashyaTarget: The rulings of רבה and רב המנונא on an אתרוג that crosses a year boundary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא requires both growth and picking in the obligated period, so both cases are exempt from both laws. That contradicts any ruling that obligates these cases.

steps.title: The ברייתא Contradicts רב המנונא, and Partly רבה
steps.stepSummary: The first case of the ברייתא contradicts רב המנונא, who obligates it in מעשר. The second case contradicts both רבה and רב המנונא, who obligate it in ביעור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is difficult for רב המנונא. The latter clause is difficult for both רבה and רב המנונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא states exactly whose opinion each half of the ברייתא contradicts. This finishes the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רישא: the ברייתא exempts the sixth-into-seventh אתרוג from מעשר. רבה agrees, but רב המנונא said it is obligated. סיפא: the ברייתא exempts the seventh-into-eighth אתרוג from ביעור. Both רבה and רב המנונא said it is obligated in ביעור, so both are challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of a source.
The latter clause of a source.
It is a difficulty.
For both this one and that one.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says obligation requires both growth and picking in the obligated year. It agrees with רבה on the first case's מעשר exemption, but it goes against both רבה and רב המנונא on ביעור for fruit picked in the eighth year.

phrases.english: The first clause is difficult for Rav Hamnuna,
phrases.notes: He obligates the sixth-into-seventh etrog in tithes.

phrases.aramaic: סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבָּה בֵּין לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא!
phrases.english: the latter clause is difficult for both Rabba and Rav Hamnuna!
phrases.notes: Both obligate the seventh-into-eighth etrog in elimination.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא קַשְׁיָא לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא, סֵיפָא קַשְׁיָא בֵּין לְרַבָּה בֵּין לְרַב הַמְנוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא from step 15 to the two opinions and says exactly whom it contradicts.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא on מעשר in the first case; רבה and רב המנונא on ביעור in the second case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא's exemptions directly contradict the obligations that these Amoraim ruled.

steps.title: The answer: this is a dispute among the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רבה and רב המנונא by saying that רבי שמעון's ruling is only one side of a dispute among תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute among the תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from רבי שמעון's ברייתא. It says the תנאים themselves disagree, so רבה and רב המנונא may simply follow a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אמורא is not refuted by a ברייתא if other תנאים disagree with that ברייתא. The גמרא is about to bring a source showing that such a disagreement exists about the אתרוג.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute among the תנאים (the Sages of the משנה era)
A Sage of the משנה period

phrases.english: It is a dispute of the Tannaim.
phrases.notes: The אמוראים follow a different tannaic opinion, not רבי שמעון's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 16 from רבי שמעון's ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Tannaic dispute: the contradicting source is only one side of an argument among תנאים.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי שמעון's ברייתא seemed to disprove רבה and רב המנונא outright.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי שמעון's view is not the only tannaic view. רבה and רב המנונא can rely on another opinion.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the five elders and the vote at אושא
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records two tannaic positions on the אתרוג. The five elders say it follows its picking for מעשר. The Sages at אושא say it follows its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught in a ברייתא: רבי יוסי said, אבטולמוס testified in the name of five elders that an אתרוג follows its picking for מעשר. Our Rabbis voted in אושא and said it follows its picking for both מעשר and שביעית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows the תנאים disagree. There are two opinions about whether the picking time decides the אתרוג's year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The five elders mention picking only for מעשר. This implies that for שביעית they hold the אתרוג follows its formation (חנטה), which fits רבה and רב המנונא. The Sages at אושא make picking decide both laws, which is a different view.

keyTerms.meaning: A Sage who testified to an older tradition
Testified, meaning he passed on a received tradition
Picking (harvesting) of the fruit
They voted or counted heads to decide the law
Town in the Galil where the Sanhedrin met after the destruction

steps.confusionAlert: The five elders say nothing directly about שביעית. Their view on שביעית is only implied, and the next step questions exactly this.

phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Yosei said,
Avtolemos testified in the name of five elders:
An etrog follows its picking for tithes,
phrases.notes: For מעשר, the year of picking decides.

phrases.english: but our Rabbis voted in Usha and said:

phrases.aramaic: אַחַר לְקִיטָתוֹ, בֵּין לְמַעֲשֵׂר בֵּין לִשְׁבִיעִית.
phrases.english: It follows its picking, both for tithes and for the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: The Sages at אושא make picking decide both laws.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim in Step 17 that the תנאים disagree.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the law of the אתרוג is a dispute among תנאים.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי יוסי, which records the testimony of אבטולמוס and the vote at אושא.

steps.title: Why is שביעית mentioned at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the Sages at אושא speak about שביעית, when the five elders only spoke about מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the wording of the ברייתא. The first opinion talked only about מעשר, so it asks why the second opinion brings in שביעית. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the five elders never mentioned שביעית, the phrase 'both for מעשר and for שביעית' at אושא seems to answer a point nobody made. The גמרא wants to know what the five elders held about שביעית, so the two opinions really line up as a dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: Who mentioned its name? (a phrase showing that a topic appears out of nowhere)
The Sabbatical Year and its laws, such as ביעור

phrases.english: Who mentioned anything about the Sabbatical Year?
phrases.notes: The first opinion spoke only about מעשר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the wording of the ברייתא brought in Step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the ruling at אושא mention שביעית when the five elders discussed only מעשר? What did the five elders hold about שביעית?
